comments.body: Another from tooling feedback, 2026-10-16 (0.16.0, devenv): `muster pane send --pane p2bjgf98za --enter --confirm "/compact"` into an idle Codex. Codex took it and compacted (`pane read` showed "Compacting context", then "Context 0% used"), but send printed "the text was sent ... and does not show on it any more than it did before, so whatever is running there did not take it", with three causes that did not apply. It is the same shape as `/quit`: a consumed slash command leaves the prompt empty.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Landed 2026-10-16: --confirm now answers unknown (exit 4) when the pane changed without showing the text - a consumed slash command, a quit, a submitted prompt - and refuses (exit 1) only when nothing changed or the line was cut short. Nothing that was refused became confirmed, so a_2hIfvZQJP is not reopened.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
GitHub issue #2 part 10: `pane send --confirm` reports that Codex did not take `/quit` when it did. After `muster pane send --pane <id> "/quit" --enter --confirm`, Codex took `/quit` and exited to the shell prompt, but send reported:

```
the text was sent to pane <id> and does not show on it any more than it did before, so whatever is running there did not take it
```

followed by three possible causes, none of which applied. Taken at its word, the next step is to resend or press keys, which would type into the shell.

The check seems to look for the sent text on screen, which misfires whenever a program consumes the line and redraws: a quit, a slash command, a cleared prompt. Treating a changed screen, or a change in the pane's foreground process, as taken, and warning only when nothing on the pane changed, would fix it. It is not Codex-only. A tooling-feedback report saw it with Claude Code 2.1.296 and ordinary prompt text: `--confirm --enter` in one call exited 1 about 0.5 s after the previous turn's Stop, roughly once in 60 sends, while a UserPromptSubmit hook proved the prompt was submitted. `CONFIRM_WITHIN` is 1 s. Where the pane changed but the text cannot be found, reporting "unknown" (exit 4, as an unanswered send does) is more honest than "did not take it". The message comes from `crates/muster-core/src/pane_text.rs`. Earlier `--confirm` fixes (cards a_2cW56wz6X, a_2MGkaw6H5) are worth reading first so this does not undo them.

The opposite failure, `--confirm` passing for text that then vanished from a busy Claude Code pane, is card `pane-send-confirm-passed`; a fix to one should not reopen the other.
title: pane send --confirm says a program did not take a line it took and redrew
